title: Solid circular shaft in torsion, axisymmetric with twist (Saint-Venant)
source: Saint-Venant torsion of a circular shaft, Timoshenko and Goodier, Theory of Elasticity, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill 1970, ch. 10

quantities.quantity: displacement along Z, −r θ for a right-handed twist θ about +Y, at the surface of the loaded end (r = 20, axial position 100)
quantities.reason: the bilinear element on a rectangle holds u_θ = κ r z and its 2 × 2 rule integrates the forces of τ_zθ exactly, so the result is the closed form (negative: a torque about +Y turns +X toward -Z, u_z = -r kappa y) to the round-off of the solve

quantities.quantity: shear stress τ_zθ at the surface at mid length (stress component 6, yz)
quantities.reason: the bilinear element on a rectangle holds u_θ = κ r z and its 2 × 2 rule integrates the forces of τ_zθ exactly, so the result is the closed form (negative: a torque about +Y turns +X toward -Z, u_z = -r kappa y) to the round-off of the solve

quantities.quantity: shear stress τ_rθ at the same point (stress component 5, xz)
quantities.reason: zero in the closed form; 10⁻⁶ MPa is round-off at a stress of 80 MPa
